title: Serving Runtime — staff huddle (bridge) 2026-04-28
content:
ATTENDEES: Marco, Priya, Dylan, Hannah, Elena, Sam (SRE), Lisa (Platform eng). 6 total.

TL;DR:
- Short action: pause the zstd quantized-kernel rollout for 2 days while we investigate ~15ms p95 regressions seen in small query loads. (Decision: PR revert+hotfix queued).
- Canary of v1.38 runtime continues in us-west-2 but we've reduced traffic by 30% and enabled strict fallbacks.
- Incident review: two customer sandboxes showed elevated tail latency during autoscale; root cause likely related to recent batching change + cold KV cache priming.
- Ops: monthly maintenance window scheduled May 2 01:00-03:00 UTC; notify Dedicated customers and check SLA calendar.

NOTES / DISCUSSION POINTS:
1) zstd kernel rollout (Dylan)
   - Observed: after enabling zstd quantization path, internal warm-load benchmarks show 8–20% CPU reduction but p95 increased by ~10–15ms on model M-XL when batch < 4.
   - Hypothesis: kernel path reduces compute per-token but interacts with the runtime's micro-batching heuristics; small-batch latency suffers because of new memcopy pattern.
   - Decision: pause rollout, revert PR 1284 for now. Dylan to open a targeted perf investigation ticket (INFR-4123) and add microbenchmark harness.
   - Action: Dylan assigned, due 2026-04-30. Priya to prepare communication draft for customers using quantized variants.

2) Canary status and traffic shaping (Priya)
   - Canary v1.38 in us-west-2. Traffic routed only from internal services + 10% of beta customers.
   - Metrics: request success 99.91%, 95th latency 74ms overall, but us-west-2 canary hosts show a 12ms tail delta versus baseline.
   - Mitigation: reduced traffic by 30%, strict fallback to v1.37 on latency spike. Continue close monitoring; escalate if regressions persist > 6h.

3) Autoscale/tail latency incident (Hannah / SRE)
   - Summary: two customer-dev sandboxes experienced 4x queue depth spikes during a morning growth pulse; autoscaler added nodes but warm KV priming + cache cold starts led to tail latency bursts.
   - Root cause candidates: batching threshold change (PR RUNTIME-289) + aggressive scale-in policy left minimal warmed capacity.
   - Short-term fix: relax scale-in to 5m from 2m for sandbox clusters; add jitter to priming job.
   - Long-term: implement warm-pool target and predictive pre-warm based on request patterns (backlog for Q2).
   - Action: Hannah to file change to scale-in policy and measure for 48h (due 2026-04-30). Sam to run additional load tests mirroring customer profile.

4) Cost optimization highlight (Elena)
   - Early Redwood Optimize suggestion reduced token-cost on a demo workload by 6% (batching + cache TTL tweaks). Consider packaging as a ‘starter-config’ for PLG signups.
   - Action: Elena to produce a one-pager w/ cost delta and config snippets (due 2026-05-05).

5) Upcoming maintenance (Marco)
   - Planned: kernel upgrade + node OS patch May 2 01:00-03:00 UTC. Dedicated customers need targeted notices.
   - Checklist: backup canary configs, snapshot KV caches, notify SRE on call. Lisa to coordinate customer comms and add to status.redwood page.
   - Action: Lisa assigned (due 2026-04-30).

DECISIONS MADE:
- Pause zstd quantized-kernel rollout and revert PR to staging until micro-benchmark confirms no small-batch p95 regressions.
- Reduce canary traffic by 30% and enable immediate fallback policy for v1.38.
- Temporarily relax scale-in to reduce cold-start tail for sandboxes.

ACTION ITEMS (owner / due):
- Dylan: open perf-investigation ticket INFR-4123 + microbenchmark harness (due 2026-04-30).
- Priya: customer-facing draft about zstd pause + FAQ (due 2026-04-30).
- Hannah: change scale-in policy to 5m and run 48h check (due 2026-04-30).
- Sam (SRE): run repro load tests for sandbox pattern and log findings (due 2026-04-29).
- Elena: cost-optimization one-pager for PLG onboarding (due 2026-05-05).
- Lisa: maintenance comms and status page update (due 2026-04-30).

BLOCKERS / PARKING LOT:
- Need a reliable small-batch microbenchmark harness that simulates 50–200 concurrent tiny requests — current harness focuses on larger batches. (Tech debt for perf infra.)
- Dependence on kernel dev team bandwidth next sprint; may push zstd work into mid-May.
- Unresolved: how to expose fallback metrics cleanly in Console (Marco to scope with product).

METRICS SNAPSHOT (most recent 30m):
- Global RPS: 8.2k (up 6% w/w).
- Average token/sec per GPU: 11.8k.
- p50/p95/p99 latency (text-gen): 12ms / 74ms / 210ms.
- Error rate: 0.09% (steady).
- Node utilization (serving pool): 68% avg, 92% peak.

MEETING NOTES (verbatim highlights / quick quotables):
- "We bought CPU savings but lost 15ms at small batch — that math doesn't help a latency-sensitive checkout flow." — Priya
- "If fallbacks are seamless we can be more aggressive in canary, but we haven't surface-tested failover paths enough." — Hannah
- "We should have a single place that maps rollout flags -> customer impacts (dashboard)." — Marco

FOLLOWUPS / NEXT STEPS:
- Next cross-team staff check-in: 2026-05-05 09:30 PT. Agenda: zstd perf findings, canary health after rollback, maintenance readiness.
- Folks: drop any experimental logs / flamegraph excerpts into the shared folder (Confluence link in linked_artifacts). Priya will collate and post a summary before next meeting.

NOTES TO SELF (informal):
- Remember to ping legal for Dedicated customer maintenance notices if any regulatory customer affected.
- Revisit batching heuristics — maybe consider an adaptive threshold for small-batch fast-path.
- Add a single metric in Console for "fallback-rate" per route.

END.

(attachment idea: short csv with canary host latencies + CPU; will add to linked_artifacts once generated)
